words: The main argument in favour of friends is that they provide enjoyment and shared interests.
This is because we choose friends who share our hobbies, tastes and values.
For example, teenagers select friends to socialise and have fun with.
As a result, friendships create happiness and memorable experiences throughout life.
rounds.note: Topic sentence → reason (This is because …) → example (For example …) → result (As a result …).

words: In the first place, I believe that sport develops crucial skills in teamwork and collaboration.
This is because organised games teach students to coordinate and resolve conflicts constructively.
To illustrate, students in regular team sport demonstrate stronger interpersonal skills in the classroom too.
Consequently, the social benefits of school sport extend beyond the playing field.
rounds.note: Topic sentence → reason (This is because …) → example (To illustrate …) → result (Consequently …).

words: Another point that supports my view is that professional athletes display remarkable dedication and hard work.
This is because achieving elite status demands decades of intensive training and sacrifice.
For instance, professional competitors devote countless hours to demanding physical preparation.
Thus, their commitment and sacrifices merit appropriate recognition.
rounds.note: Topic sentence → reason (This is because …) → example (For instance …) → result (Thus …).

words: For one thing, I believe that helping friends and family significantly strengthens personal relationships.
This is because supporting others builds trust, respect and deeper emotional connections.
For example, helping a friend during difficult times brings people much closer together.
As a result, relationships become stronger, more reliable and more meaningful.
rounds.note: Topic sentence → reason (This is because …) → example (For example …) → result (As a result …).

words: For one thing, I believe that language study delivers authentic enjoyment and intellectual satisfaction.
This is because exploring new linguistic systems provides fascinating mental stimulation.
To illustrate, using foreign languages during travel produces incredibly enriching experiences.
Consequently, language learning transforms into something deeply fulfilling and worthwhile.
rounds.note: Topic sentence → reason (This is because …) → example (To illustrate …) → result (Consequently …).

words: A further contributing factor is social comparison with others online.
This happens because people constantly see idealised images of others' seemingly perfect lives.
For instance, teenagers compare themselves to influencers and celebrities.
Consequently, feelings of inadequacy and low self-esteem develop rapidly.
rounds.note: Topic sentence → reason (This happens because …) → example (For instance …) → result (Consequently …).

words: One positive aspect of internet learning is remarkable flexibility and access.
This is because pupils can engage with lessons at any time from any location.
For example, students review recorded content during periods convenient for them.
Therefore, educational opportunities expand for those with complex schedules.
rounds.note: Topic sentence → reason (This is because …) → example (For example …) → result (Therefore …).

words: Another possibility is that technological progress promises better and safer working conditions.
This is because intelligent machines will take over tasks that are gruelling or genuinely dangerous.
For instance, mining robots already spare workers from hazardous environments.
Thus, automation will protect human health and dignity in the workplace.
rounds.note: Topic sentence → reason (This is because …) → example (For instance …) → result (Thus …).

words: Another point that supports my view is that caring for a pet creates a meaningful sense of purpose and routine.
This is because animals depend on their owners for food and exercise.
For instance, walking a dog every morning gives owners a consistent daily structure.
Consequently, people develop healthier habits.
rounds.note: Topic sentence → reason (This is because …) → example (For instance …) → result (Consequently …).

words: First of all, the main reason I hold this view is that advertising does provide useful information about products and services.
This is because businesses use ads to announce new products and promotional offers.
To illustrate, consumers discover helpful innovations and savings opportunities through advertisements.
Consequently, shoppers can make slightly better-informed purchasing choices.
rounds.note: Topic sentence → reason (This is because …) → example (To illustrate …) → result (Consequently …).

words: Another point that supports my view is that fast fashion damages the environment significantly.
This is because cheap, disposable clothing creates enormous amounts of waste globally.
For example, millions of tonnes of unwanted clothes end up in landfills annually.
Therefore, the environmental cost is absolutely devastating for our planet.
rounds.note: Topic sentence → reason (This is because …) → example (For example …) → result (Therefore …).

words: Another major issue is that industrial pollution and plastic contaminate water bodies extensively.
This is because manufacturing plants discharge poisonous substances directly into natural waterways.
For instance, enormous quantities of marine wildlife die from ingesting plastic waste yearly.
Thus, vital ocean and river ecosystems suffer devastating harm.
rounds.note: Topic sentence → reason (This is because …) → example (For instance …) → result (Thus …).

words: It seems clear to me that eliminating commuting time is a huge advantage.
This is because home workers avoid lengthy daily journeys to workplaces.
For example, employees often save multiple hours each day previously lost to travel.
Therefore, they feel less exhausted and more energised.
rounds.note: Topic sentence → reason (This is because …) → example (For example …) → result (Therefore …).

words: In addition, government policies and incentives have accelerated adoption.
This is because many governments offer tax reductions and subsidies to encourage switching.
For instance, several European countries plan to ban new petrol car sales within the next decade.
Consequently, electric vehicles are rapidly becoming the mainstream choice globally.
rounds.note: Topic sentence → reason (This is because …) → example (For instance …) → result (Consequently …).

words: What is more, I feel strongly that there are compelling reasons to protect these animals.
This is because every species plays vital roles in maintaining natural balance.
For instance, bees pollinate crops that humans depend on for food.
Consequently, losing animal species threatens our own survival too.
rounds.note: Topic sentence → reason (This is because …) → example (For instance …) → result (Consequently …).

words: One positive aspect of being self-employed is having complete independence and control.
This is because independent workers make autonomous decisions about schedules, assignments and clientele.
For example, self-employed professionals work during their peak effectiveness periods.
Therefore, career fulfilment and drive commonly improve dramatically.
rounds.note: Topic sentence → reason (This is because …) → example (For example …) → result (Therefore …).

words: The main advantage of taking a gap year is acquiring meaningful experience and personal independence.
This is because travelling, volunteering or working abroad builds character and useful capabilities.
For example, young people managing life in foreign countries develop excellent self-sufficiency.
Therefore, they frequently excel academically upon resuming their education.
rounds.note: Topic sentence → reason (This is because …) → example (For example …) → result (Therefore …).

words: Moreover, lack of physical exercise contributes significantly to rising obesity rates.
This is because children spend hours on screens instead of playing outdoors actively.
For instance, many prefer video games to sports or cycling.
Consequently, fitness levels have declined sharply among young people.
rounds.note: Topic sentence → reason (This is because …) → example (For instance …) → result (Consequently …).

words: Another point that supports my view is that entertainment options have expanded enormously.
This is because streaming platforms provide unlimited access to films and music instantly.
For instance, we can enjoy any content from home at any time.
Consequently, people have far more ways to relax and enjoy themselves.
rounds.note: Topic sentence → reason (This is because …) → example (For instance …) → result (Consequently …).

words: A further reason is that advertising aimed at children encourages unnecessary spending.
This is because young children are particularly susceptible to persuasive marketing techniques.
For instance, children who see toy adverts frequently pressure their parents into purchases they cannot afford.
Consequently, such advertising creates significant financial stress for families.
rounds.note: Topic sentence → reason (This is because …) → example (For instance …) → result (Consequently …).

words: The main argument in favour of modern technology is its ability to connect people regardless of location.
This is because messaging apps and social networks enable instant global communication.
To illustrate, families living on different continents can video chat regularly and remain closely involved in each other's lives.
Consequently, geographical separation no longer prevents close relationships.
rounds.note: Topic sentence → reason (This is because …) → example (To illustrate …) → result (Consequently …).

words: An additional consideration is that concentrating solely on tomorrow neglects essential understanding of today.
This is because historical knowledge provides necessary frameworks for interpreting present circumstances.
For instance, contemporary politics becomes comprehensible only with historical foundation.
Thus, knowledgeable citizens form better judgments on significant questions.
rounds.note: Topic sentence → reason (This is because …) → example (For instance …) → result (Thus …).

words: The main argument in favour of larger families is that children develop excellent social abilities through sibling relationships.
This is because growing up with brothers and sisters teaches sharing, teamwork and compromise.
To illustrate, older children frequently mentor and support their younger siblings.
Consequently, they grow into less self-centred and more socially skilled individuals.
